title: H3b v3: wire decision routes into the daemon (spec reviews T-0430 and T-0434 folded in) — shared failures module breaks the import cycle, per-task packet sections under one goal claim, off-tick close gate after the dedup check, bounded PR-create failure handling, cursor per goal with cursor_at_launch on records
spec:
Replaces T-0433 (T-0365 before it) after spec reviews T-0430 and T-0434. Build on goal/T-0353 (H3a decision.py, H2 launch attribution, H7 failure kinds and signatures, H6 acceptance gate, G7 v4 auto fix rounds, G8 semantic triggers merged; H4 reservations merging).
1. Shared helpers, no import cycle: new module orchestrator/failures.py holding the pure and bus-only helpers both daemon.py and planner_runs.py need: test id extraction from failure text (the H6/H7 validated extractor), rejecting_reviews(task), path_in_scope(path, scope), failure_kind, failure_signature, changed_paths and the unified-diff helper, touch_areas(task) with the [review.areas] tables. failures.py imports only bus, spawn, merge and stdlib, never daemon or planner_runs; daemon.py re-exports or calls them (existing names keep working, existing tests untouched); planner_runs.build_ctx imports failures at module scope. No deferred imports of daemon inside planner_runs.
2. build_ctx(point) fills every field decision.route reads (decision.py lines 84-148) from these sources: routes = [planner.routes]; infra_failure_kind = quota | auth | unavailable from the pool's cooldown or usage-limit reason for the account or executor involved or pipeline.failure_kind quota/permissions, else None (present); premium_launches = escalate launches recorded for the goal. held: failing_ids (failures extractor over resume_hint.failures), in_scope_review_comments (every rejecting review comment path inside scope), auto_fix_rounds_used (lineage count of constraints.auto_round), auto_fix_rounds ([daemon].auto_fix_rounds), failure_signature, signature_repeated (equals an earlier lineage signature), spec_review_request_changes (spec_review tasks with inputs[0] in the lineage and verdict request_changes), blocked_scouts (scout ids under the goal with status blocked), touches_auth/migrations/interfaces/data_deletion (touch_areas; unavailable diff sets all four True). scouts_done: goal_complexity, scout_count, all_scouts_posted, blocked_scouts from the bus; security_trigger = any goal scope path matches [review].security_paths; semantic_trigger = goal spec or scope matches [review].semantic_paths or semantic_patterns. closable: all_children_merged (every execute child done with merged_into); gate_state from the cached close gate (item 4): green | red | unknown.
3. Claims and packets: one claim record per goal launch, kind "goal", payload_key = state_version (sha12 over sorted (task id, status, hold_reason, merged_into, last event seq) of the goal's children); _blocked and gave_up apply to it; per-point records remain history; the module docstring documents the scheme. The dedup check on state_version runs before any other work for that goal in the tick. Packet: one section per held task that routes to escalate (hold_reason, failing ids, review comments, branch and head sha, route reason, evidence, cheaper steps) plus one section for scouts_done when present; held tasks that route to routine are excluded from the packet (auto_fix_round handles them) and never trigger a launch on their own; an identical state_version never launches twice; unrelated goals never share a packet; a blocked scout or a security hold launches in the same tick as its point. Test with two simultaneously held siblings under one goal, one routine-fixable and one escalate-worthy: exactly one launch whose packet carries only the escalate sibling, and the routine sibling gets its automatic fix round.
4. Closable: after the dedup check passes and all children are merged, the daemon dispatches the goal-head gate off-tick via spawn_async (a fresh worktree at the goal head, tests-green bounded by [limits].timeout_s.execute) and records pipeline.close_gate = {sha, state, ts} on the GOAL task; build_ctx reads that cache for the current head sha and reports unknown until it lands; unknown means no launch and no rerun in the same tick; the gate is rerun only when the head sha changes. Routine close (gate green, everything merged) runs off-tick too: stamp(goal, "closed_at") under bus.locked() first, then idempotent effects each checked by evidence before acting: retrospective entry (record script, or the no-new-learning marker) present in decisions.md; PR exists (gh pr list --head goal/<id> --json url) else gh pr create from the fixed template; GOAL result posted with pr_url. gh failures: record pipeline.close_error with the message, notify once per transition, retry on a later tick after [daemon].close_retry_s (default 900) up to [daemon].close_max_attempts (default 3), then route escalate with reason close_failed; gh failures never count toward the launch gave_up counter; a crash between the stamp and an effect is reconciled by the same evidence checks.
5. investigate launches on [planner.routes].investigate_tier, escalate on the premium tier; route, reason, evidence, cheaper_steps into the claim record (H2 fields); [planner.routes].enabled = false restores per-point escalation. Infra failures (auth, quota, unavailable markers) set a pool cooldown with reason, do not count toward gave_up, notify once per transition, and leave the cursor unchanged. Soft premium budget: exceeding [planner.routes].premium_launches_soft_per_goal still launches and records exception: true.
6. Cursor: one per-goal processed-event cursor lives in planner_runs.json (goal_cursors[goal_id]); it advances only after a launch is recorded as started; each launch record carries cursor_at_launch (the value read when its packet was built) for attribution.
Tests in tests/test_planner_runs.py, tests/test_daemon.py and tests/test_failures.py: test_failures_module_has_no_daemon_import, test_ctx_fields_complete_for_each_kind, test_routine_hold_launches_no_model, test_two_held_siblings_one_packet_only_escalate_section, test_closable_gate_runs_off_tick_once_per_head, test_closable_unknown_gate_launches_nothing, test_closable_routine_is_idempotent_across_ticks, test_close_gh_failure_retries_then_escalates_without_gave_up, test_investigate_uses_smaller_tier, test_escalate_uses_premium_tier_with_reason, test_same_state_version_never_relaunches, test_two_goals_two_packets, test_cursor_advances_only_after_launch_start, test_auth_failure_cools_account_without_gave_up, test_soft_budget_exceeded_still_launches_with_exception, test_routes_disabled_restores_per_point_launch, test_touch_areas_fail_closed_without_diff. Keep every existing test green; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0; git add -A and commit with the task id; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: tests/test_failures.py::test_failures_module_has_no_daemon_import passes and grep shows planner_runs.py imports failures at module scope and never imports daemon

tests/test_planner_runs.py and tests/test_daemon.py: test_ctx_fields_complete_for_each_kind, test_routine_hold_launches_no_model, test_two_held_siblings_one_packet_only_escalate_section, test_closable_gate_runs_off_tick_once_per_head, test_closable_unknown_gate_launches_nothing, test_closable_routine_is_idempotent_across_ticks, test_close_gh_failure_retries_then_escalates_without_gave_up, test_investigate_uses_smaller_tier, test_escalate_uses_premium_tier_with_reason, test_same_state_version_never_relaunches, test_two_goals_two_packets, test_cursor_advances_only_after_launch_start, test_auth_failure_cools_account_without_gave_up, test_soft_budget_exceeded_still_launches_with_exception, test_routes_disabled_restores_per_point_launch, test_touch_areas_fail_closed_without_diff pass

every launch record carries route, reason, evidence, cheaper_steps, state_version and cursor_at_launch; planner_runs.json holds goal_cursors per goal; the routine close stamps closed_at before any side effect
pool.toml documents [review.areas], [daemon].close_retry_s and close_max_attempts; the planner_runs module docstring documents the goal-record claim scheme
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

events.reason: superseded by T-0437 (the registered Planner session, server pid 7181, wrote an equivalent H3b v3 that resolves spec review T-0434 with gate_state from merge evidence and no suite run); this session (Claude Code pid 6410) yields the goal

spec_review_risks.issue: failures.py must hold changed_paths and 'the unified-diff helper' (daemon.py's _added_diff_lines, line 836), but both depend on _resolve_base (line 459) and _git_in (line 442). The spec's helper list for failures.py never mentions moving these, and failures.py is forbidden from importing daemon. An executor either duplicates git-subprocess logic in two modules or fails test_failures_module_has_no_daemon_import.

run() and reconcile() currently do a deferred `from . import daemon` (lines 513, 720) solely to call daemon.notify() on gave_up. The spec demands 'No deferred imports of daemon inside planner_runs' plus a grep-checked acceptance criterion that planner_runs never imports daemon, but failures.py's helper list has no notify() replacement, so satisfying the letter of the spec silently drops gave_up notifications.

Item 3 replaces per-(goal_id,kind,payload_key) dedup with a single goal-level claim keyed by a state_version hash over all children, aggregated into one packet. decision_points()/_blocked()/run() (lines 201, 168, 454) and ~43 existing tests (e.g. test_decision_points_scouts_done_held_closable, test_held_key_changes_with_each_new_hold, test_run_launches_once_per_key) assert the current independent per-kind model directly. The spec never states whether the old model is removed or kept alongside the new one -- kept side by side risks double-launching a headless Planner for the same held task (once via the legacy 'held' point, once via the new packet); removed, it breaks the 'keep every existing test green' requirement.

decision.py (out of scope, unmodifiable) routes closable's gate_state='unknown' to result('escalate', 'unknown:gate_state') at lines 146-149, and per item 5 escalate always launches on the premium tier. Item 4 explicitly requires 'unknown means no launch and no rerun in the same tick,' but the spec never says build_ctx/the caller must short-circuit before calling decision.route() for that state -- a naive wiring launches a premium-tier Planner every tick until the off-tick gate lands.

Item 4 has daemon.py itself run `gh pr list`/`gh pr create` and post the GOAL result off-tick with no LLM or human step -- there is no existing gh automation anywhere in the repo today (zero grep hits), and CLAUDE.md step 8 currently has the Planner (an agent) open goal/<parent> -> main. This spec quietly moves that decision into deterministic daemon code with automatic retries, without calling out that this is a policy/autonomy change.
